clue.text: Practised one of the 3Rs vocally as a way of learning

indicators.note: vocally says the word for the practised skill is to be heard spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: the 3 Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic; having practised writing, you wrote

explanation.surface: A pupil who drilled one of the basic school skills out loud, as a method of study.
explanation.walkthrough: The 3 Rs are the old phrase for basic schooling: reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning by rote means memorising through repetition, a familiar method of study.

clue.text: Gear to have on when holding a party or dance

parts.note: rig is gear or equipment
a do is a party
taken as written

explanation.surface: Clothes to wear while hosting a celebration or a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear to have on' reads as clothing; 'Gear' is RIG and 'on' holds A + DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigadoon is a lively Provençal dance of the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: A tinker's set, out from former homeland

indicators.note: set out means the letters of a tinker's are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A travelling mender's equipment leaves its old country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges A TINKERS; 'set' looks like the tinker's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Transkei was a nominally independent black homeland in apartheid South Africa.

clue.text: Publicity is not half wanted by : Mary, a right madam?

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of the word is is kept

parts.note: the Madonna is the Virgin Mary

explanation.surface: A publicist wonders whether a bossy woman called Mary wants press coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half of 'is', I, is kept. 'wanted by' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna is a temperamental, self-important woman, which is what a right madam is in British slang.

clue.text: Looking healthy, blooming!

definitions.meaning: a mild British exclamation of annoyance, like bloody

explanation.surface: Someone is in the pink, in rude good health.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a reddish, healthy complexion, and a mild British substitute for bloody.

clue.text: Way Navy is facing change, ultimately to adapt to today's world

parts.note: a mode is a way
RN is the Royal Navy
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of change

explanation.surface: The navy faces change as it adapts to the modern era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' is only a link here; 'ultimately' gives E, the last letter of 'change'.
explanation.definitionFit: To modernise is to bring something up to date, suited to the present day.

clue.text: There may be another killing after this — scene at the end is ghastly

definitions.text: There may be another killing after this

indicators.note: ghastly says the letters of scene at the end are horribly mangled

explanation.surface: A grisly final scene in a murder drama promises further deaths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ghastly' rearranges SCENE AT THE END. The definition: a court's sentence of execution leads to another killing.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital sentence orders an execution, a further killing after the murder that prompted it.

clue.text: See silly person strip in the kitchen

definitions.meaning: a long thin strip of pasta made in the kitchen

explanation.surface: Look at the fool undressing in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link pointing to the first sense. 'strip' looks like undressing; it is a ribbon of pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a fool or simpleton, and a long ribbon of pasta.

clue.text: Very keen to have paintings round the study

indicators.note: round says the paintings word encircles the study word

parts.note: paintings are art
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: An enthusiast wants pictures hung all around the study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the container signal; 'study' is a cosy private room here, not the act of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate or eager, so very keen.

clue.text: Looked quickly in church being overwhelmed by organ

indicators.note: the church abbreviation is engulfed, swallowed up, by the organ word, so it goes inside

parts.note: a gland is a bodily organ
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone peeked swiftly while in church, drowned out by the organ music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the church instrument, but it is a body part; 'being overwhelmed by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance is to look briefly and quickly, so glanced is the past tense synonym.

clue.text: Sure thing, one lies about a legal document!

parts.note: a cert is a certainty, a sure thing
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about says the lies word goes around the letter a

parts.note: fiction is untruth, lies

explanation.surface: Someone tells lies about a legal document, which is a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts FICTION around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A certification is an official certificate attesting to a fact.

clue.text: Something precious no girl turned and rejected ultimately?

indicators.note: turned tells us the pair no plus girl is read from the back

parts.note: taken as written
a maid is a girl in old usage

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of rejected

explanation.surface: A precious gift that no young woman would turn away?
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses NO + MAID to give DIAMON; 'ultimately' adds D, the last letter of 'rejected'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond is a gemstone, the classic example of a precious thing.

clue.text: Wrecker of some French city once having monarch

parts.note: des is French for of some
Troy is the ancient city of legend
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: Someone who ruined a French city in the days when it had a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French city' tempts as a single piece, but 'of some French' gives DES and 'city once' the ancient TROY.
explanation.definitionFit: A destroyer is one who destroys, so a wrecker of things; also a warship.

clue.text: Constantine's mother, not a beautiful woman

indicators.note: not says the letter given by the word a is left out

parts.note: St Helena was the mother of the Roman emperor Constantine

explanation.surface: A remark that the emperor's mother was no beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' removes A from HELENA, mother of Constantine the Great.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen of Troy is the archetypal beauty, so the name stands for a lovely woman.

clue.text: Turning to one of our pages for info about when to go to pubs?

definitions.text: Turning to one of our pages
definitions.meaning: the clue is printed in the Times newspaper, so turning to its pages is opening that paper

definitions.text: info about when to go to pubs?
definitions.meaning: the hours during which pubs are serving customers

explanation.surface: A newspaper reader flips to a page to find out when the pubs are open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our pages' means those of the newspaper printing the puzzle, The Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Licensing hours, when establishments may serve customers, are their posted schedule of trade.

clue.text: Georgia, upper-class girl showing awkwardness

parts.note: GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia
U means upper-class in British usage
Cherie is a girl's name, French for darling

explanation.surface: A posh girl from Georgia is clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' is a link. U as upper-class comes from 1950s British debate about U and non-U speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaucherie means tactless or socially awkward behaviour.

clue.text: With the day halfway, through, assess flood

indicators.note: halfway says only half of the named day is kept

parts.note: Saturday, a day of the week
to rate is to assess

explanation.surface: Halfway through the day, someone judges how much flooding there is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halfway' keeps SATU, the first half of SATURDAY. 'With' and 'through' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To saturate is to soak completely, to flood with liquid.

clue.text: Musical phrase isn't a too awful construction

indicators.note: an awful construction is a poorly built arrangement, so the letters of isn't a too are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A tune that is not, after all, too badly put together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful construction' rearranges ISNT A TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostinato is a short musical phrase repeated persistently.

clue.text: Pieces of meat quick in the cooking, and maybe in the eating!

definitions.text: Pieces of meat quick in the cooking, and maybe in the eating!

parts.words: Pieces of meat quick in the cooking, and maybe in the eating!
parts.note: thin cuts of beef that fry in a moment, and the small portion suggests they vanish just as fast

explanation.surface: Thin cuts of beef cook fast and are wolfed down just as fast.
explanation.definitionFit: These thin beef cuts are named for cooking in about sixty seconds, the smallest unit on a clock dial.

clue.text: Youngster: tot locked in lounge?

indicators.note: locked in says the tot word is shut inside the lounge word

parts.note: to lie is to lounge
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A toddler shut in the sitting room?
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a child and 'lounge' a room; they are verbs, ADD and LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A laddie is a young lad, Scots for a boy.

clue.text: Sent on a particular course, getting 'beaten

explanation.surface: Someone sent along a set path ends up thrashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: directed by a chosen path, and soundly defeated in battle.

clue.text: Marketplace traversed by Pythagoras?

indicators.note: traversed by says the letters run straight through the philosopher's name

explanation.surface: Did the Greek philosopher walk across the market square?
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits within PythAGORAs, a fitting place for a Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the public square and market of an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Unreliable chum, lion — may eat you finally, little people!

indicators.note: may eat says the rearranged letters take in, swallow, the final letter
unreliable suggests the letters of chum and lion cannot be trusted to stay put
finally picks the last letter of you

explanation.surface: A warning that a fickle friend and a lion could devour you in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unreliable' is the anagram signal; 'may eat' puts the last letter of 'you' inside the rearranged letters. 'little people' points to the alchemists' tiny men.
explanation.definitionFit: Homunculi are tiny men or manikins, in alchemy and folklore.

clue.text: Supreme leader of Eastern state

parts.note: main means chief, supreme

indicators.note: leader of picks the opening letter of Eastern

explanation.surface: The top man of an eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supreme leader' reads as one title; it splits into MAIN and the first letter of 'Eastern'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a US state in New England.

clue.text: More eccentric little girl having row

parts.note: Dot is a short name for Dorothy, a girl's name
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A small girl having a quarrel is rather odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a line of seats, TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty means slightly mad or eccentric, so the comparative is dottier.

clue.text: Overcoming veto, I parrot artistic arrangement

indicators.note: overcoming suggests the bird word goes over and around the veto word

parts.note: the kea is a New Zealand parrot
a ban is a veto

explanation.surface: A man defies a prohibition and makes his parrot do art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parrot' looks like a verb, to copy, but it is the bird KEA, which holds BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of flower arranging.

clue.text: Eden, garden sadly put at risk

indicators.note: sadly means the letters of Eden and garden are in a sorry, disordered state

explanation.surface: The biblical paradise garden is, alas, under threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges EDEN GARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Endangered means exposed to danger or threatened, especially of species.

clue.text: Fellow on the fiddle, remarkable person first to last

indicators.note: first to last says the opening letter is shifted to the end of the word

parts.note: a oner is British slang for a remarkable person

explanation.surface: A swindling man, an outstanding character who went from first to last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' suggests cheating, but it is the emperor who fiddled while Rome burned. ONER is British slang for someone exceptional.
explanation.definitionFit: Emperor Nero reputedly played the fiddle while Rome burned.
